findings.title: Rework is moved-head re-verification: 15 of 20 extra review rounds; one-round yield 0.8125 vs 0.963
findings.claim: Over the 80 window merges that carry a verdict, 15 of the 20 verdicts after a merge's first re-verified a head that moved after a `merge` verdict, and all 15 returned `merge`. Only 3 extra rounds were repairs after a block, and 1 of those blocks was an engineering class. So the brief's first-pass yield (0.963) counts as first-pass 12 merges that were reviewed two or three times; the one-round yield is 0.8125.
findings.mechanism: orchestrator.md s11 requires a merge verdict from a reviewer that measured THIS head, and fixer.md re-executes steps 2-8 after any rebase or merge. So a head that moves after `merge` (origin/main merged in: 6; a bot autofix commit such as `ci: drop inherited claims` or a closures re-record: 3; a content commit after the verdict: 6) costs one more full review round. First-verdict yield counts none of these rounds, and policy_lint.mjs:statsHistogram's `head-moved` row (19) puts them in one cell with the 3 repair rounds and 1 duplicate same-head post.

findings.title: Owner-approved (code-owned) merges skip the fix verdict: 8 of 22 carry none, against 0 of 66 app-approved
findings.claim: All 8 of the window's 88 merges that carry no `Fix review:` verdict on either endpoint went through the owner-approval path (APPROVED review by the code owner): 8 of 22 owner-approved merges, against 0 of 66 hpo-approver merges. No rule in the tree exempts that class: orchestrator.md s11 requires a merge verdict at the merged head before every merge, and CLAUDE.md makes the owner the approver for code-owned paths, not the fix reviewer.
findings.mechanism: Approval and verdict are separate gates. The app path cannot approve without a verdict (app_approve.sh is keyed on the verdict's SHA), so that arm is 0/66. The owner's review satisfies the code-owner rule without one, so nothing forces a verdict on that arm. The brief's title-prefix classes spread these 8 across fix-and-feature (3) and record-and-chore (5); the approval path is the variable that separates them.
